## SCI-ATOM-001

**Lyα (H I 1s → 2p) transition data** — ✓ verified · domain: atomic

**Claim.** Neutral hydrogen in its ground state resonantly absorbs Lyα photons at a rest (vacuum) wavelength of 1215.67 Å, with absorption oscillator strength f ≈ 0.4164; the 2p level decays back to 1s with Einstein coefficient A21 ≈ 6.26×10⁸ s⁻¹, i.e. a lifetime ≈ 1.6 ns.

**Equations.**

$$ \lambda_0 = 1215.6701\ \text{Å (vacuum)},\quad f_{12} = 0.4164,\quad A_{21} = 6.2649\times10^{8}\ {\rm s^{-1}} $$

**Convention.** λ0 = 1215.6701 Å is NIST's unresolved 1s–2 multiplet value (its upper level includes 2s); the gf-weighted 2p centre is 1215.67004 Å (0.015 km/s different). The ~1.3 km/s fine-structure splitting (1215.6736 / 1215.6682 Å) is below every width the resource shows and is not taught.

**Teaching representation.** one resonance, "one colour in the atom's own frame" (Beat 2)

**Validity.** all IGM conditions considered (A₂₁ far exceeds the collisional and photo-excitation rates at IGM densities, so n = 2 is essentially empty)

**Assumptions.** vacuum wavelengths; fine structure unresolved; ground-state population only

**Sources.**

- primary: Kramida, A., Ralchenko, Yu., Reader, J., and NIST ASD Team (2024). NIST Atomic Spectra Database (ver. 5.12), https://physics.nist.gov/asd [accessed 2026-10-02]. National Institute of Standards and Technology, Gaithersburg, MD. — H I lines output 1215–1216 Å (2p3/2, 2p1/2, unresolved 1s–2) ✓
- primary: Wiese, W. L. & Fuhr, J. R. 2009, J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 38, 565–720, 'Accurate Atomic Transition Probabilities for Hydrogen, Helium, and Lithium'; Publisher's Note: J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 38, 1129 (2009) — Table 6, entry 1, p. 578 (λ 1215.67 Å, A = 6.2649e8 s⁻¹, f = 0.41641, g 2–6) ✓

**Oracle.**  values typed independently in a separate Python check and compared in VAL-TAU-001 (constants)

**Implementation.** `science/js/lyaphys.js` — C.lambda_A, C.f, C.A21

**Validation.**

- VAL-TAU-001: τ of single, blended, saturated, damped, under-resolved and periodic lines vs exact-Voigt oracle; ∫τ du; τ0; wing τ=1 width — **pass** · 8/8 checks; point sampling max rel τ 5.0e-05, max |ΔF| 1.8e-05

**Scenes using this claim** (derived): Beat 2 · One atom meets one colour, Beat 4 · The atom's lifetime leaves faint, far wings, Beat 5 · The same colour, stretched, Beat 13 · Same shadow

## SCI-ATOM-002

**Resonance in the atom's frame (Doppler condition)** — ✓ verified · domain: atomic / kinematics

**Claim.** An atom moving with line-of-sight velocity v sees incoming light Doppler-shifted; it is resonant with light whose observed (lab-frame) wavelength is λ0(1 + v/c) to first order in v/c. An atom moving away from the observer (v > 0, toward the quasar) therefore absorbs a redder colour.

**Equations.**

$$ \lambda_{\rm res} = \lambda_0\,(1 + v/c) + \mathcal{O}(v^2/c^2) $$

**Convention.** same sign as SCI-MAP-003

**Teaching representation.** "Which atoms bring this colour into resonance in their frame?" (Beat 2); ticks shifting in the atom-frame panel

**Validity.** v ≪ c

**Assumptions.** non-relativistic speeds (v/c ≲ 10⁻³)

**Deliberate simplifications / exaggerations.**

- The resonance window is drawn ~500× wider than the natural width (see SCI-REP-004).

**Sources.**

- primary: Rybicki, G. B. & Lightman, A. P. 1979, Radiative Processes in Astrophysics (New York: Wiley); Wiley-VCH reprint 2004 — §10.6 Line Broadening Mechanisms — Doppler broadening, p. 287 ✓

**Oracle.**  VAL-MAP-001 checks that v_pec > 0 gives larger u and longer λ_obs (sign test)

**Implementation.** `science/js/lyaphys.js` — uOfX, lambdaObs

**Validation.**

- VAL-MAP-001: map u(x): independent formula, h-independence, sign, constant-H validity vs exact distance–redshift, λ_obs convention — **pass** · 5/5 checks; linear map vs exact over 20 Mpc/h: 2.0e-03

**Scenes using this claim** (derived): Beat 2 · One atom meets one colour

**Interactive controls acting through this claim** (derived): INT-ATOMV-001 (Beat 2): the atom's speed along the beam v [km/s] (v > 0 away from us)

## SCI-RES-001

**Lyα "absorption" in the IGM is resonant scattering out of the beam** — ✓ verified · domain: radiative transfer

**Claim.** After excitation to 2p the atom decays radiatively (A21 ≫ collisional and photo-excitation rates at IGM densities), re-emitting a Lyα photon in an essentially random direction. For a narrow beam from a point source this removes the photon from the line of sight; scattering of other photons into the beam is negligible. The beam's extinction therefore obeys the same e^−τ law as true absorption.

**Equations.**

$$ 1s + \gamma_{\rm Ly\alpha} \to 2p \to 1s + \gamma\ (\text{random direction}) $$

**Convention.** Say "scattered out of our beam" in Beat 2 and again in Beat 5, where "shadow" is introduced; "removed"/"absorbed" elsewhere as shorthand.

**Teaching representation.** the resonant photon leaves the beam at an angle (Beat 2 animation)

**Validity.** quasar sightlines through the diffuse IGM

**Assumptions.** point source; beam solid angle ≪ 4π; negligible re-scattering into the beam

**Deliberate simplifications / exaggerations.**

- Later beats say "absorbed" for brevity.

**Sources.**

- primary: Meiksin, A. A. 2009, Rev. Mod. Phys. 81, 1405–1469, 'The physics of the intergalactic medium' — §I footnote 7; §II.A opening (features are scattering of resonance photons out of the line of sight) ✓
- secondary: Dijkstra, M. 2014, PASA 31, e040, 'Lyα Emitting Galaxies as a Probe of Reionisation' — §4 Lyα Radiative Transfer Basics, opening paragraph; §5.2 ✓

**Scenes using this claim** (derived): Beat 2 · One atom meets one colour

## SCI-THERM-001

**Maxwellian velocities; one line-of-sight component is Gaussian** — ✓ verified · domain: statistical mechanics

**Claim.** In gas at temperature T each Cartesian velocity component of the atoms follows a Gaussian with variance kT/m. The beam is sensitive only to the component along it.

**Equations.**

$$ f(v_\parallel) = \sqrt{\frac{m}{2\pi kT}}\;e^{-m v_\parallel^2/2kT} $$

**Convention.** v_∥ along the sightline, positive away from the observer

**Teaching representation.** representative atoms with line-of-sight arrows; each atom's arrow travels down to one speed ruler, tail at zero, and leaves a mark at its speed; the marks form a band and stack into the census (Beat 3, VT-THERM-WRITE / VT-THERM-CENSUS; micro "why a Gaussian?")

**Validity.** IGM gas (collisional thermalisation of velocities is fast compared with dynamical times)

**Assumptions.** thermal equilibrium of the atoms' motions; no turbulence

**Deliberate simplifications / exaggerations.**

- A few hundred representative atoms stand in for ~10⁶⁶ (SCI-REP-001).

**Sources.**

- primary: Rybicki, G. B. & Lightman, A. P. 1979, Radiative Processes in Astrophysics (New York: Wiley); Wiley-VCH reprint 2004 — §10.6 Line Broadening Mechanisms — Doppler broadening, p. 287 ✓

## SCI-THERM-002

**Doppler parameter and the thermal (Gaussian) profile** — ✓ verified · domain: line formation

**Claim.** The census of line-of-sight speeds is the line's thermal profile: a Gaussian in Δv of width b = √(2kT/m), normalised so that heating spreads the same absorption over more velocities without adding any. b(10⁴ K) = 12.85 km/s for hydrogen.

**Equations.**

$$ b = \sqrt{2kT/m_{\rm H} + b_{\rm turb}^2},\qquad \phi_{\rm G}(\Delta v) = \frac{e^{-\Delta v^2/b^2}}{\sqrt{\pi}\,b} $$

**Convention.** m = mass of the ¹H atom (1.00782503 u = 1.6735328×10⁻²⁴ g; an earlier value, 1.6735575×10⁻²⁴ g, was corrected — a 1.5×10⁻⁵ effect); b_turb = 0 unless stated. (fake_spectra's mass convention is recorded in SCI-SIM-002.)

**Teaching representation.** temperature control → arrows → marks → census → the census curve drops into the line profile, the same shape now in optical depth at a fixed amount of hydrogen (Beat 3, VT-THERM-LINE)

**Validity.** all thermal widths considered

**Assumptions.** Maxwellian velocities (SCI-THERM-001)

**Deliberate simplifications / exaggerations.**

- Turbulent / unresolved bulk motion inside a parcel is ignored in the toy (b_turb = 0); in real lines it adds in quadrature.
- Beat 3 isolates the intrinsic thermal Doppler width. A real absorber's line is also widened by velocity variation across the extended gas — the Hubble flow and its own motions across its size (SCI-REP-003, shown in Beat 6) — and the recorded line by the instrument (SCI-OBS-001, Beat 11). A line width alone is therefore not a thermometer (SCI-DEG-001).

**Sources.**

- primary: Rybicki, G. B. & Lightman, A. P. 1979, Radiative Processes in Astrophysics (New York: Wiley); Wiley-VCH reprint 2004 — §10.6 Line Broadening Mechanisms — Doppler broadening, p. 287 ✓
- secondary: Draine, B. T. 2011, Physics of the Interstellar and Intergalactic Medium (Princeton University Press) — ch. 6, §6.5 (p. 58) ✓
- secondary: Meiksin, A. A. 2009, Rev. Mod. Phys. 81, 1405–1469, 'The physics of the intergalactic medium' — §II.A, Eqs. (10)–(11): b = (2kT/m_a)^½; a kinematic component adds in quadrature ✓

**Oracle.**  VAL-TAU-001 checks τ0 and ∫τ du, which fix the normalisation (analytic)

**Implementation.** `science/js/lyaphys.js` — dopplerB, tau0

**Validation.**

- VAL-TAU-001: τ of single, blended, saturated, damped, under-resolved and periodic lines vs exact-Voigt oracle; ∫τ du; τ0; wing τ=1 width — **pass** · 8/8 checks; point sampling max rel τ 5.0e-05, max |ΔF| 1.8e-05

**Scenes using this claim** (derived): Beat 3 · Temperature becomes line width, Beat 6 · Where does one parcel land?, Beat 13 · Same shadow

## SCI-NAT-001

**Natural broadening from the finite lifetime of 2p** — ✓ verified · domain: atomic / radiation

**Claim.** Because the 2p state has a finite lifetime (1/A21 ≈ 1.6 ns), even a stationary atom's response is a Lorentzian with half-width γ = Γλ0/4π ≈ 0.0061 km/s, Γ = A21 (2p decays only to 1s). This is 1765× narrower (FWHM) than the thermal width at 10⁴ K, but falls off only as 1/Δv².

**Equations.**

$$ \gamma = \frac{\Gamma\lambda_0}{4\pi} = 6.06\times10^{-3}\ {\rm km\,s^{-1}},\qquad a = \gamma/b $$

**Convention.** Γ is the total decay rate out of the upper level (the lower level is the ground state, width 0)

**Teaching representation.** Beat 4 in four steps: exponential survival of 2p → a very narrow natural line → invisible inside the thermal core → its wings win far out. The classical damped oscillator and its Lorentzian spectrum are in the Beat 4 microscope only.

**Validity.** IGM densities (n ≲ 10⁻² cm⁻³)

**Assumptions.** radiative damping only; collisional (pressure) broadening negligible at IGM densities

**Deliberate simplifications / exaggerations.**

- The damped oscillation (microscope only, labelled) is the classical Lorentz-oscillator analogue; the physical statement is the finite lifetime.
- The natural line is magnified ×1200 in the inset (SCI-REP-004).

**Sources.**

- primary: Rybicki, G. B. & Lightman, A. P. 1979, Radiative Processes in Astrophysics (New York: Wiley); Wiley-VCH reprint 2004 — §10.6 — natural broadening (Lorentzian) ✓

**Oracle.**  γ_v recomputed independently in a separate Python check; VAL-TAU-001 (constants)

**Implementation.** `science/js/lyaphys.js` — C.gamma_kms, aDamp

**Validation.**

- VAL-TAU-001: τ of single, blended, saturated, damped, under-resolved and periodic lines vs exact-Voigt oracle; ∫τ du; τ0; wing τ=1 width — **pass** · 8/8 checks; point sampling max rel τ 5.0e-05, max |ΔF| 1.8e-05

**Scenes using this claim** (derived): Beat 4 · The atom's lifetime leaves faint, far wings

## SCI-VOIGT-001

**The Voigt profile — normalisation, definition and asymptotics** — ✓ verified · domain: line formation

**Claim.** The line profile is the convolution of the thermal Gaussian with the natural Lorentzian (each atom's Lorentzian at each atom's Doppler shift). In velocity units φ(Δv) = H(a, Δv/b)/(√π b), with H(a,x) = Re w(x + ia) and ∫H dx = √π. For a ≪ 1 the core is ≈ e^(−x²) and the far wings ≈ a/(√π x²): core from motion, wings from lifetime.

**Equations.**

$$ H(a,x) = \frac{a}{\pi}\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\frac{e^{-y^2}\,dy}{(x-y)^2 + a^2},\qquad \phi(\Delta v) = \frac{H(a,\Delta v/b)}{\sqrt{\pi}\,b} $$
$$ H(a,x) \simeq e^{-x^2} + \frac{a}{\sqrt{\pi}\,x^2}\quad (a \ll 1) $$

**Convention.** x = Δv/b, a = γ/b

**Teaching representation.** "Two thousand times narrower — but it never lets go"; core/wings shading on a log scale (Beat 4); stamping micro view

**Validity.** all a considered; the two-term asymptotic is a teaching approximation, not used in computation

**Assumptions.** SCI-THERM-002 and SCI-NAT-001 act independently (impact approximation not needed)

**Deliberate simplifications / exaggerations.**

- The micro view exaggerates the damping parameter (labelled, ×1–1000).

**Sources.**

- primary: Rybicki, G. B. & Lightman, A. P. 1979, Radiative Processes in Astrophysics (New York: Wiley); Wiley-VCH reprint 2004 — §10.6 — combined Doppler and Lorentz profiles (Voigt) ✓
- primary: Meiksin, A. A. 2009, Rev. Mod. Phys. 81, 1405–1469, 'The physics of the intergalactic medium' — §II.A, Eqs. (9)–(13): Voigt = Lorentzian ⊗ Maxwellian; H(a,x); a ✓

**Oracle.** scipy.special.wofz (SciPy 1.15.2; Faddeeva package, S. G. Johnson) scipy.special.wofz (Faddeeva function) (numerical)

**Implementation.** `science/js/lyaphys.js` — voigtH, phiV

**Validation.**

- VAL-VOIGT-001: browser H(a,x) vs scipy wofz on a 42×321 grid, a ∈ [1e-6,1], x ∈ [0,2e4] — **pass** · max relative error 8.5e-05 over 13482 grid points (physical a (1e-4 ≤ a ≤ 6.1e-3), core |x| ≤ 4: 5.0e-05; physical a, wings 4 < |x| ≤ 2e4: 4.9e-05; tiny a (1e-6 ≤ a < 1e-4), all x: 5.0e-05; teaching exaggeration (6.1e-3 < a ≤ 1), all x: 8.5e-05)

## SCI-RED-001

**Cosmological redshift stretches every wavelength by the same factor** — ✓ verified · domain: cosmology / frames

**Claim.** Light absorbed by gas at redshift z_abs at rest-frame wavelength λ_rest (1215.67 Å for Lyα, in the gas's own frame) reaches us at λ_obs = λ_rest (1 + z_abs), where 1 + z_abs = a(t_obs)/a(t_abs). Every wavelength, and every wavelength interval, is multiplied by the same factor. The reverse operation, λ_rest = λ_obs/(1 + z_abs), re-expresses the observed spectrum in the absorber's rest frame: there the absorber's own line is at exactly 1215.67 Å. (In the quasar's rest frame, λ_obs/(1 + z_q), the same absorption lies blueward of 1215.67 Å — SCI-RED-002.)

**Equations.**

$$ \lambda_{\rm obs} = \lambda_{\rm rest}(1+z),\qquad 1+z = \frac{\lambda_{\rm obs}}{\lambda_{\rm rest}} = \frac{a(t_{\rm obs})}{a(t_{\rm em})},\qquad \lambda_{\rm rest} = \frac{\lambda_{\rm obs}}{1+z} $$

**Convention.** Three frames are kept distinct: the absorber's rest frame (where the atom sees 1215.67 Å), the observer's frame (us), and the quasar's rest frame (SCI-RED-002). "Measured at a point along the path" means by an observer at rest with the cosmic expansion there (comoving), for whom λ ∝ a.

**Teaching representation.** Beat 5: the quasar's spectrum is a ribbon, carrying its own labels, that stretches against a ruler of wavelength measured where the light is; "show the physics" re-expresses the recorded spectrum in the selected structure's or the quasar's rest frame. In review probes 3–4 the reader squeezes the recorded spectrum by hand: undoing a stretch is a uniform compression about 0 Å, never past the quasar's own frame (VT-RED-UNDO).

**Validity.** any z; the beat uses 0 ≤ z_abs < z_q = 3.2 with z = 3 as the default (the toy's redshift)

**Assumptions.** FLRW expansion; comoving observers; the gas's own small motion folded into z_abs here

**Deliberate simplifications / exaggerations.**

- Redshift is presented as the stretching of the light's wavelength with the expansion (λ ∝ a); the Doppler-vs-expansion interpretation debate is not raised.

**Sources.**

- primary: Hogg, D. W. 1999, 'Distance measures in cosmology', arXiv:astro-ph/9905116 (v4, 16 Dec 2000); pedagogical note, not published in a journal — §3 'Redshift', Eq. (8): z = λ_o/λ_e − 1; Eq. (12): 1 + z = a(t_o)/a(t_e) ✓

**Oracle.** science/oracle/mapping_oracle.py and science/oracle/redshift_oracle.py (scipy quad + brentq) frame conversions computed directly from 1 + z = λ_obs/λ_rest (science/oracle/redshift_oracle.py) (numerical)

**Implementation.** `science/js/lyaphys.js` — stretch, lambdaObsOfRest, lambdaRestOfObs

**Validation.**

- VAL-RED-001: frames and redshift: χ(z) and z(χ) vs scipy (Planck 2018 and old toy cosmology), λ_obs = λ_rest(1+z) and its reverse, quasar frame blueward, log-λ stretch = velocity on the SCI-MAP-004 axis, the forest written along the way (λ_emit, λ_here = 1215.67 Å at z_abs, λ_obs, ordering) — **pass** · 6/6 checks; χ(z) vs scipy max rel 8e-11; z(χ) inverse 2e-09; frame conversions exact to 1e-16; Lyα at z = 3 → 4862.68 Å

**Scenes using this claim** (derived): Beat 5 · The same colour, stretched

## SCI-RED-002

**The quasar's frame — why the forest lies blueward of the quasar's own Lyα** — ✓ verified · domain: cosmology / frames

**Claim.** The quasar at z_q emits its own Lyα at 1215.67 Å in its frame, observed at 1215.67 (1 + z_q) Å. Gas between us and the quasar (z_abs < z_q) absorbs at 1215.67 (1 + z_abs) Å observed, i.e. at 1215.67 (1 + z_abs)/(1 + z_q) < 1215.67 Å in the quasar's rest frame: the Lyα forest lies blueward of the quasar's Lyα emission.

**Equations.**

$$ \lambda_{\rm q} = \frac{\lambda_{\rm obs}}{1+z_{\rm q}} = 1215.67\,\text{Å}\,\frac{1+z_{\rm abs}}{1+z_{\rm q}} < 1215.67\,\text{Å}\quad (z_{\rm abs} < z_{\rm q}) $$

**Convention.** SCI-RED-001

**Teaching representation.** Beat 5 — a quiet graphite anchor, the quasar's own Lyα, rides on the ribbon from step 1 (it leaves the Lyα mark at the quasar and drifts redward ahead of every shadow, VT-RED-ANCHOR); "show the physics" re-expresses the recorded spectrum in the quasar's rest frame, with its Lyα emission drawn, and the whole forest sits blueward of the anchor

**Validity.** z_abs < z_q

**Assumptions.** absorbers lie between us and the quasar

**Deliberate simplifications / exaggerations.**

- The quasar's emission line is drawn as a smooth bump on a flat continuum; its real shape and the proximity zone are not shown.

**Sources.**

- primary: Meiksin, A. A. 2009, Rev. Mod. Phys. 81, 1405–1469, 'The physics of the intergalactic medium' — §II.A 'Resonance absorption lines', text preceding Eq. (15) (arXiv v3 p. 7); §I, p. 2 (absorption shortward of the QSO's Lyα) ✓

- secondary: Rauch, M. 1998, ARA&A 36, 267–316, 'The Lyman Alpha Forest in the Spectra of Quasistellar Objects' — §1 Introduction, first paragraph (preprint p. 3), stated in words ✓

**On a logarithmic ruler a stretch is a slide; small slides are velocities** — ✓ numeric · source-location pending · domain: cosmology / conventions

**Claim.** Because the stretch multiplies every wavelength by (1 + z), it adds the same amount, ln(1 + z), to every ln λ. Small differences in ln λ are velocities, Δu = c Δln λ; this is the velocity coordinate u used from Beat 6 on, with λ_obs = λ0 (1 + z0) e^(u/c) (SCI-MAP-004).

## SCI-RED-005

**The forest is written along the way** — ✓ verified · domain: cosmology / radiative transfer

**Claim.** As the quasar's light travels, its wavelength measured by local comoving observers grows, λ_here = λ_emit (1 + z_q)/(1 + z_here). Each intervening hydrogen structure at z_abs absorbs the part of the spectrum that is at 1215.67 Å in its own frame — the part emitted at λ_emit = 1215.67 (1 + z_abs)/(1 + z_q) — and that shadow then stretches on with the light, reaching us at 1215.67 (1 + z_abs). Structures at different redshifts therefore cast shadows at different observed wavelengths, ordered by redshift, all blueward of the quasar's own Lyα at 1215.67 (1 + z_q): the Lyα forest.

**Equations.**

$$ \lambda_{\rm here} = \lambda_{\rm emit}\,\frac{1+z_{\rm q}}{1+z_{\rm here}},\qquad \lambda_{\rm emit} = 1215.67\,\text{Å}\,\frac{1+z_{\rm abs}}{1+z_{\rm q}}\ \Rightarrow\ \lambda_{\rm obs} = 1215.67\,\text{Å}\,(1+z_{\rm abs}) $$

**Convention.** SCI-RED-001; one redshift per structure (peculiar motion folded in, separated in SCI-MAP-001)

**Teaching representation.** Beat 5: continuous gas along the line of sight; a fixed Lyα mark on the ruler of wavelength measured where the light is; the whole ribbon stretches past it as the light travels; every bit of gas writes at the mark (density peaks darkly); earlier shadows keep moving redward; a close-up of the mark shows the first shadows drifting; the journey accelerates into a forest.

**Validity.** z_abs < z_q

**Assumptions.** absorbers between us and the quasar; Lyα only

**Deliberate simplifications / exaggerations.**

- Lyβ and higher Lyman lines, the Lyman limit, and the atmospheric cut-off are not drawn.

**Sources.**

- primary: Meiksin, A. A. 2009, Rev. Mod. Phys. 81, 1405–1469, 'The physics of the intergalactic medium' — §II.A 'Resonance absorption lines', text preceding Eq. (15) (arXiv v3 p. 7): absorption appears at observed wavelengths between λ_lu and λ_lu a(t)/a(t₀) ✓

## SCI-MAP-001

**Real space → velocity space map** — ✓ verified · domain: cosmology / kinematics

**Claim.** Gas at comoving position x along the sightline, with line-of-sight peculiar velocity v_pec, absorbs at velocity coordinate u = aH(z) x_com + v_pec. Across a box of tens of Mpc/h the expansion rate is treated as constant.

**Equations.**

$$ u(x) = a(z)H(z)\,x_{\rm com} + v_{\rm pec}(x) = \frac{100\,E(z)}{1+z}\,x\,[{\rm Mpc}/h]\ \ {\rm km\,s^{-1}},\qquad E = \sqrt{\Omega_m(1+z)^3 + \Omega_\Lambda} $$

**Convention.** flat ΛCDM, radiation neglected; Planck 2018 (Ωm = 0.3153, ΩΛ = 0.6847, h = 0.6736) gives 114.19 km/s per Mpc/h at z = 3

**Teaching representation.** Hubble-aligned rulers; fine threads from each parcel sub-cell's real-space position to where it lands in velocity space — straight under expansion alone, tilting, crossing and folding with peculiar velocity (Beat 7, VT-MAP-FIBRES); pencil ghosts at the Hubble-only position; Beat 12 traces a colour back along the same map

**Validity.** boxes ≲ 100 Mpc/h at z ≈ 2–4 (the linear map deviates from the exact distance–redshift map by 1.0% at 100 Mpc/h; VAL-MAP-001)

**Assumptions.** constant H across the box (SCI-MAP-005); first order in v/c

**Deliberate simplifications / exaggerations.**

- Beat 7 shows velocities relative to the near edge of the stretch (an additive constant).

**Sources.**

- primary: Hui, L., Gnedin, N. Y. & Zhang, Y. 1997, ApJ 486, 599–622, 'The Statistics of Density Peaks and the Column Density Distribution of the Lyα Forest' — §2, Eq. (3): u = H̄(x − x̄)/(1+z̄) + v_pec, x comoving ✓
- primary: Bird, S., Haehnelt, M., Neeleman, M., Genel, S., Vogelsberger, M. & Hernquist, L. 2015, MNRAS 447, 1834–1846, 'Reproducing the kinematics of damped Lyman α systems' — §2.6, Eqs. (6)–(7) (fake_spectra) ✓
- secondary: Meiksin, A. A. 2009, Rev. Mod. Phys. 81, 1405–1469, 'The physics of the intergalactic medium' — §VI.C.1, Eq. (104); §II.A (ordered flow shifts the line centre) ✓

**Oracle.** science/oracle/mapping_oracle.py and science/oracle/redshift_oracle.py (scipy quad + brentq) comoving-distance integration (science/oracle/mapping_oracle.py) (numerical)

**Implementation.** `science/js/lyaphys.js` — hubblePerMpch, uOfX

## SCI-MAP-002

**Comoving vs physical coordinates and h-units** — ✓ verified · domain: conventions

**Claim.** Positions are comoving (Mpc/h); a column density uses the proper path length Δx_prop = a·Δx_com/h (in cm); velocities are physical km/s; densities are proper cm⁻³. The velocity per comoving Mpc/h, aH(z)/h = 100E(z)/(1+z), does not depend on h.

**Equations.**

$$ N_j = n_{{\rm HI},j}\;\Delta x_{\rm prop},\quad \Delta x_{\rm prop} = \frac{a\,\Delta x_{\rm com}[{\rm Mpc}/h]}{h}\,{\rm Mpc} $$

**Convention.** as stated

**Teaching representation.** ruler labels "comoving Mpc/h" and "km/s"

## SCI-MAP-004

**Velocity coordinate ↔ observed wavelength** — ✓ verified · domain: conventions

**Claim.** The velocity ruler is converted to observed wavelength with λ_obs = λ0(1+z0)e^(u/c) (the log-λ convention); to first order this equals λ0(1+z0)(1+u/c). Over 20 Mpc/h at z = 3 the two differ by 2.9e-05 in 1+z.

**Equations.**

$$ \lambda_{\rm obs} = \lambda_0\,(1+z_0)\,e^{u/c} $$

## SCI-MAP-006

**Velocity-gradient (Hubble) broadening of an extended absorber** — ✓ verified · domain: cosmology / kinematics

**Claim.** Gas that is extended along the line of sight spreads its absorption in velocity: the Hubble flow across its depth, and any internal peculiar-velocity gradient, give its parts different line-of-sight velocities, and this bulk spread adds to the thermal motion of its atoms. For a Gaussian clump of width σ_x with a linear velocity field, the spread is a Gaussian of dispersion |aH + dv/dx|·σ_x, i.e. a Doppler parameter b_size = √2·|aH + dv/dx|·σ_x, which adds in quadrature to the thermal b; this expression is the resource's own algebra (a Gaussian velocity spread convolved with the thermal Gaussian), checked analytically and by VAL-ORTH-001 — the sources give the physics, not the formula. In CDM collapse models the low-column-density forest clouds are cool but large, so this term can dominate their widths.

**Equations.**

$$ b^2 = b_{\rm thermal}^2 + b_{\rm size}^2,\qquad b_{\rm size} = \sqrt{2}\,\left|aH + \tfrac{dv}{dx}\right|\sigma_x $$

**Convention.** x comoving in Mpc/h, aH in km/s per Mpc/h (SCI-MAP-001); σ_x the clump's 1σ width along the beam

**Teaching representation.** the parcel's width in Beats 6–8; the clouds of Beat 13

**Validity.** smooth, single-stream flow across the clump (SCI-TAU-004); a real absorber's flow need not be linear

**Assumptions.** Gaussian density profile along the beam; a linear velocity field across it; one temperature

**Sources.**

- primary: Rauch, M. 1998, ARA&A 36, 267–316, 'The Lyman Alpha Forest in the Spectra of Quasistellar Objects' — §3.3 (arXiv v1 p. 14): in CDM collapse models, low-column clouds are cool but large, 'so that the Hubble expansion dominates the line broadening' ✓
- primary: Meiksin, A. A. 2009, Rev. Mod. Phys. 81, 1405–1469, 'The physics of the intergalactic medium' — §II.A, Eqs. (10)–(11): b = (2kT/m_a)^½; a kinematic component adds in quadrature ✓

**Oracle.**  a Gaussian velocity spread convolved with a Gaussian thermal profile is a Gaussian whose b² is the sum; VAL-ORTH-001 checks the drawn width against it (analytic)

**Implementation.** `science/js/lyaphys.js` — parcelToCells, parcelWidths

**Validation.**

- VAL-ORTH-001: Beat 6's four teaching dimensions stay separate: place, own motion, temperature and neutral amount each changed alone across its control's domain (read from the manifest), checked on the parcel's cells (u, b, N) and on its optical depth (lyaphys parcelTau, measured with lineMoments: centre, FWHM, area) on a fine grid and on the scene's own grid (the comparison it prints); what it prints about the width (b6reading): thermal b, the size term √2·aH·σ_x, and the drawn line's b and peak measured on its drawn grid, against the fine grid and the quadrature sum; flux nonlinearity under saturation recorded, not tested — **pass** · 91/91 checks over 18 one-variable changes (cells and τ, fine grid and the scene's grid): place and motion move the centre by aH·Δx and Δv (max error 4e-07 km/s) at fixed FWHM and area; temperature changes FWHM² by 4 ln2 Δ(b²) (max rel. error 1e-04) at fixed centre and area; amount scales τ exactly (max rel. 2e-15) at fixed centre and FWHM. The width the scene prints is the drawn line's: heat alone b = 21.4 km/s and the parcel's size 23.8 km/s add in quadrature to the drawn 32.0 km/s (max rel. error 2e-04; peak 3e-04). Flux is not linear (recorded): N_HI ×2 gives τ area ×2 but equivalent width ×1.19 (τ₀ = 4.4); T ×2 at fixed N_HI changes it ×1.13

**Scenes using this claim** (derived): Beat 6 · Where does one parcel land?, Beat 13 · Same shadow

## SCI-TAU-001

**Optical depth of one absorber** — ✓ verified · domain: radiative transfer

**Claim.** An absorber of neutral column N_HI has τ(Δv) = N σ_v φ(Δv) with σ_v = (πe²/m_e c) f λ0 = 1.3435×10⁻¹² cm² km/s, so ∫τ dv = N σ_v (independent of temperature) and the Doppler line-centre value is τ0 = 0.758 (N/10¹³)(10 km/s / b).

**Equations.**

$$ \tau(\Delta v) = N_{\rm HI}\,\sigma_v\,\phi(\Delta v),\quad \sigma_v = \frac{\pi e^2}{m_e c}f\lambda_0,\quad \tau_0 = \frac{N\sigma_v}{\sqrt\pi\,b} $$

**Convention.** velocity-space cross-section (cm² km/s); φ normalised to 1 in km/s

**Teaching representation.** "ink = contribution to optical depth"; amount (N) vs place vs spread badges (Beat 6)

**Validity.** IGM

**Assumptions.** ground-state population only; stimulated emission negligible

**Sources.**

- primary: Rybicki, G. B. & Lightman, A. P. 1979, Radiative Processes in Astrophysics (New York: Wiley); Wiley-VCH reprint 2004 — §10.3 Einstein coefficients and oscillator strengths, p. 274 ✓
- secondary: Meiksin, A. A. 2009, Rev. Mod. Phys. 81, 1405–1469, 'The physics of the intergalactic medium' — §II.A, Eqs. (14)–(19): τ = ∫nσ ds; τ0 = Nσλ/(√π b) ✓

**Oracle.** scipy.special.wofz (SciPy 1.15.2; Faddeeva package, S. G. Johnson) science/oracle/tau_oracle.py (numerical)

**Implementation.** `science/js/lyaphys.js` — C.sigma_v, tau0, phiV

## SCI-TAU-002

**Line-of-sight accumulation of optical depth in velocity space** — ✓ verified · domain: radiative transfer / Lyα forest

**Claim.** The optical depth at velocity u is the sum (integral) over all neutral hydrogen along the sightline of each element's profile centred on its own u(x): τ(u) = ∫ n_HI σ_v φ(u − u(x); b(x)) dx_prop. Discretised on cells it is Σ_j N_j σ_v φ(u − u_j; b_j).

**Equations.**

$$ \tau(u) = \int n_{\rm HI}(x)\,\sigma_v\,\phi\bigl(u - u(x);\,b(x)\bigr)\,dx_{\rm prop}\ \approx\ \sum_j N_j\,\sigma_v\,\phi(u-u_j;b_j) $$

**Convention.** SCI-MAP-001/002/003

**Teaching representation.** "every cell: map, place its opacity, broaden, contribute" (Beat 8); stacking (Beat 9)

**Validity.** Bounded by VAL-CLOSURE-FS. For single-stream gas with b ≥ 2Δu, the app's sum matches an exact reference to 2.7e-07 in F (worst case, with fake_spectra's constants) and fake_spectra 2.2.4 to max |ΔF| 4.9e-03 (dominated by fake_spectra's H-mass convention, SCI-SIM-002); forest P1D within 0.33% (k ≤ 0.1 s/km). Outside this domain see SCI-TAU-004 (multi-stream) and SCI-TAU-005 (resolution, box).

**Assumptions.** velocity within one cell is single-valued (cell-centre; SCI-TAU-004); aH·Δx ≤ b_min/2 (SCI-TAU-005)

**Deliberate simplifications / exaggerations.**

- The app works on real-space cells; fake_spectra deposits particle kernels in velocity space (SCI-SIM-002).

## SCI-TAU-004

**One velocity per sampling element (unresolved velocity structure is not represented)** — ✓ verified · domain: radiative transfer / data

**Claim.** A real-space skewer gives each sampling element (pixel) one peculiar velocity and one temperature. If the gas inside one element has several velocities — in particle codes, several SPH particles or kernel contributions moving differently that overlap the same pixel — that sub-element velocity structure is not represented, and its absorption is placed at one velocity instead of being spread over several.

**Equations.**

$$ \tau(u) = \sum_{\rm components} \frac{n_{\rm HI}\,\sigma_v}{|du/dx|}\ \text{(cold limit)}\quad\text{vs one } u \text{ per sampling element} $$

**Convention.** SCI-MAP-001

**Teaching representation.** Implicit everywhere a place has one arrow (Beats 7–8). Stated in "show the physics" for Beat 8 as the edge of the declared domain; never shown as a student control.

**Validity.** Measured in VAL-CLOSURE-FS on synthetic configurations (largest difference in F): gas-like 1D forest 4.9e-03 (inside the tolerance); two velocity components at one position (C3c) 0.089; a velocity fold (C4c) 0.021; a 1D Zel'dovich field evolved past shell crossing (C10, a deliberately exaggerated stress test, not a claim about the IGM) up to 0.2. Any reduced sightline representation of this kind loses the velocity and density structure inside one sampling element.

**Assumptions.** one mass-weighted velocity and temperature per real-space sampling element

**Deliberate simplifications / exaggerations.**

- The toy (SCI-SIM-TOY-001) stores one mass-weighted, smoothed velocity per pixel (the Zel'dovich field is just past first shell crossing in places, but the deposit averages over it), so the app and the toy data agree by construction; the limitation matters only when comparing with particle-based codes.

**Sources.**

- primary: Hui, L., Gnedin, N. Y. & Zhang, Y. 1997, ApJ 486, 599–622, 'The Statistics of Density Peaks and the Column Density Distribution of the Lyα Forest' — §2, Eq. (5): sum over streams with |du/dx|⁻¹ ✓

**Oracle.** science/oracle/fakespectra_*.py (see closure study) cases C3c, C4c, C10 in science/validation/closure/ (numerical)

**Implementation.** `science/js/lyaphys.js` — cellsFromSkewer

**Validation.**

- VAL-CLOSURE-FS: browser real-space method vs fake_spectra 2.2.4 on controlled skewers; discrepancies decomposed by source — **pass (declared domain)** · in domain (one velocity per sampling element, b ≥ 2Δu; 25 cases): max |ΔF| 4.9e-03, |Δ⟨F⟩| 2.9e-04, |ΔEW/EW| 2.8e-03, forest P1D 0.17 % (k ≤ 0.05 s/km), 0.32 % (k ≤ 0.1); C8b compared with the exact reference (fake_spectra's own quadrature error exceeds half the tolerance). Outside the domain, stated not tolerated (max |ΔF| per test case, by case name): several velocities inside one real-space sampling element (unresolved velocity structure; C10 is a deliberately exaggerated 1D shell-crossing stress test): C10s0 0.14, C10s1 0.059, C10s2 0.13, C10s3 0.2, C3c 0.089, C4c 0.021; lines narrower than two velocity pixels (b < 2Δu); fixable by oversampling the skewer: C6a 0.45, C6b 0.21, C6c 0.049, C6d 0.46. The app's code vs its independent Python port: 6e-15 in τ

## SCI-TAU-005

**Discretisation limits — pixel size, pixel averaging and the periodic box** — ✓ verified · domain: radiative transfer / numerics

**Claim.** The cell sum is accurate only when (i) real-space pixels are finer than the narrowest line (aH·Δx ≤ b_min/2); (ii) one states whether a pixel's value is its centre τ, its mean τ or its mean F, since these differ for lines narrower than a pixel; and (iii) damping wings of strong absorbers are not cut by the periodic box.

**Equations.**

$$ aH\,\Delta x \le b_{\min}/2,\qquad \langle e^{-\tau}\rangle_{\rm pix} \ne e^{-\langle\tau\rangle_{\rm pix}} $$

**Convention.** the app's default = point sampling of τ at pixel centres on a uniform u grid; nearest periodic image per cell

**Teaching representation.** none (implementation requirement)

**Validity.** VAL-CLOSURE-FS: lines narrower than a coarse pixel are wrong by up to 0.46 in F (EW up to +93%); oversampling to aH·Δx ≤ b/2 with exact pixel averaging brings this to 0.019. The pixel-mean flux and the flux of the pixel-mean τ differ by 7e-03 to 0.31 at 10 km/s pixels (the larger for narrow saturated lines). Both codes truncate wings at half a box: for an LLS/DLA in a 5 Mpc/h box the optical depth dropped against a true periodic sum reaches 8.8. None of these occur in the toy at its sampling.

**Sources.**

- primary: fake_spectra (S. Bird), MIT license, https://github.com/sbird/fake_spectra; PyPI package 'fake_spectra' v2.2.4 — singleabs.h:104-126 (centre vs trapezoid τ); absorption.cpp:250-278 (nearest image, ±½ box) ✓

**Oracle.** science/oracle/fakespectra_*.py (see closure study) cases C6 (narrow lines), C2 (LLS/DLA wings) in science/validation/closure/ (numerical)

**Implementation.** `science/js/lyaphys.js` — tauFromCells

**Validation.**

- VAL-TAU-001: τ of single, blended, saturated, damped, under-resolved and periodic lines vs exact-Voigt oracle; ∫τ du; τ0; wing τ=1 width — **pass** · 8/8 checks; point sampling max rel τ 5.0e-05, max |ΔF| 1.8e-05
- VAL-CLOSURE-FS: browser real-space method vs fake_spectra 2.2.4 on controlled skewers; discrepancies decomposed by source — **pass (declared domain)** · in domain (one velocity per sampling element, b ≥ 2Δu; 25 cases): max |ΔF| 4.9e-03, |Δ⟨F⟩| 2.9e-04, |ΔEW/EW| 2.8e-03, forest P1D 0.17 % (k ≤ 0.05 s/km), 0.32 % (k ≤ 0.1); C8b compared with the exact reference (fake_spectra's own quadrature error exceeds half the tolerance). Outside the domain, stated not tolerated (max |ΔF| per test case, by case name): several velocities inside one real-space sampling element (unresolved velocity structure; C10 is a deliberately exaggerated 1D shell-crossing stress test): C10s0 0.14, C10s1 0.059, C10s2 0.13, C10s3 0.2, C3c 0.089, C4c 0.021; lines narrower than two velocity pixels (b < 2Δu); fixable by oversampling the skewer: C6a 0.45, C6b 0.21, C6c 0.049, C6d 0.46. ## SCI-TAU-003

**Why optical depths add** — ✓ verified · domain: radiative transfer

**Claim.** Optical depth is the path integral of the opacity; the opacity of independent absorbers (here: different gas elements at the same observed velocity) adds linearly because each atom's absorption is independent of the others and of the radiation field (no stimulated emission, no saturation of the level populations). Flux decrements do not add.

**Equations.**

$$ \tau(u) = \sum_i \tau_i(u) $$

**Teaching representation.** transparent ink layers stacking (Beat 9); the "what if dips added?" counterexample producing negative flux; Beat 12 traces one colour back — its thread splits by contribution and lands on the gas that absorbed it (VT-INV-TRACE)

**Validity.** IGM / quasar beams

**Assumptions.** linear (optically passive) medium; ground-state populations unaffected by the beam

**Sources.**

- primary: Rybicki, G. B. & Lightman, A. P. 1979, Radiative Processes in Astrophysics (New York: Wiley); Wiley-VCH reprint 2004 — §1.4, Eqs. (1.26)–(1.30): dτ = α ds ✓

**Oracle.**  VAL-TAU-001 blend case: τ of two lines = sum of individual τ (analytic)

**Implementation.** `science/js/lyaphys.js` — tauFromCells, tauContributions

**Validation.**

- VAL-TAU-001: τ of single, blended, saturated, damped, under-resolved and periodic lines vs exact-Voigt oracle; ∫τ du; τ0; wing τ=1 width — **pass** · 8/8 checks; point sampling max rel τ 5.0e-05, max |ΔF| 1.8e-05
- VAL-INV-001: inverse lookup (Beat 12): the per-cell contributions it traces sum to the spectrum's own τ at every pixel of the toy sightline; how much τ the display cut leaves untraced (it stays in the ledger's 'rest') — **pass** · Σ of traced contributions vs the spectrum's τ over 2048 pixels: max relative difference 5e-15; τ in cells under the 1% display cut (kept in the ledger's “rest”): median 3.2%, max 24.8% of a pixel's τ

## SCI-FLUX-001

**Transmitted flux (Beer–Lambert)** — ✓ verified · domain: radiative transfer

**Claim.** With no emission into the beam along the path, the transmitted fraction of the quasar's light is F = e^(−τ). F is the observed spectrum divided by the quasar's unabsorbed (continuum) spectrum.

**Equations.**

$$ F(u) = e^{-\tau(u)} $$

**Convention.** continuum-normalised flux, 0 ≤ F ≤ 1

## SCI-SAT-001

**Saturation and the curve of growth** — ✓ verified · domain: line formation

**Claim.** Once τ0 ≳ 3 the line core transmits almost nothing and the line's depth stops measuring N; its equivalent width then grows only logarithmically (∝ b√ln τ0) until the damping wings pass τ = 1, after which W ∝ √(N γ). In τ the profile shape never changes; only in F does the line change character.

**Equations.**

$$ W \propto N\ (\tau_0 \ll 1);\quad W \propto b\sqrt{\ln\tau_0}\ (\text{flat});\quad W \propto \sqrt{N\gamma}\ (\text{damped}) $$

**Teaching representation.** "Same shape in τ, a different look in F" (micro view from Beat 10)

**Validity.** isolated lines

**Assumptions.** single Voigt line

**Sources.**

- primary: Draine, B. T. 2011, Physics of the Interstellar and Intergalactic Medium (Princeton University Press) — ch. 9 Absorption Lines: The Curve of Growth (p. 75 ff.) ✓

**Oracle.** scipy.special.wofz (SciPy 1.15.2; Faddeeva package, S. G. Johnson)  (numerical)

**Validation.**

- VAL-TAU-001: τ of single, blended, saturated, damped, under-resolved and periodic lines vs exact-Voigt oracle; ∫τ du; τ0; wing τ=1 width — **pass** · 8/8 checks; point sampling max rel τ 5.0e-05, max |ΔF| 1.8e-05

**Scenes using this claim** (derived): Beat 10 · Light multiplies, Beat 13 · Same shadow

## SCI-SAT-002

**Where damping wings become visible** — ✓ verified · domain: line formation

**Claim.** From the Lorentzian asymptote, τ(Δv) ≈ Nσ_vγ/(πΔv²), so the wing reaches τ = 1 at Δv ≈ √(Nσ_vγ/π) ≈ 160 km/s (N/10¹⁹ cm⁻²)^½, independent of b (this algebra is ours, from the far-wing profile in Meiksin 2009). For forest lines (N ≲ 10¹⁵) this lies inside the Doppler core: their wings are invisible. The wings become detectable only in rare absorbers of very high column density (high N_HI).

**Equations.**

$$ \Delta v_{\tau=1} \approx \sqrt{N\sigma_v\gamma/\pi} $$

**Teaching representation.** N sweep with drop-lines from τ = 1 (micro view, Beat 10)

**Validity.** damping wings become detectable from N ≳ 10^18.5 (≈ 3×10¹⁸) cm⁻² and set the line's width at τ = 1 above about 10¹⁹ cm⁻² (the sources below); the asymptote assumes a ≪ 1

**Assumptions.** a ≪ 1

**Sources.**

- primary: Meiksin, A. A. 2009, Rev. Mod. Phys. 81, 1405–1469, 'The physics of the intergalactic medium' — §II.A, Eqs. (6), (12)–(13) and the text before Eq. (26) (arXiv v3 p. 9): far from line centre φ_V ≃ a/(πx²); §II.B.1 (p. 9): forest systems are well fit by Doppler profiles, DLAs show the damping wings ✓
- primary: Rauch, M. 1998, ARA&A 36, 267–316, 'The Lyman Alpha Forest in the Spectra of Quasistellar Objects' — §3.4 (arXiv v1 p. 15): 'From N ≳ 10^18.5 on, the damping wings of Lyα become detectable' ✓
- secondary: Wolfe, A. M., Gawiser, E. & Prochaska, J. X. 2005, ARA&A 43, 861–918, 'Damped Lyα Systems' — §1.1 (arXiv v2 p. 4): unit optical depth in the damping wings at Δν_τ=1 ∝ [A21 f21 N(H I)]^1/2 when N(H I) > 10^19 cm⁻² ✓

**Oracle.**  VAL-TAU-001: 164 vs 161 km/s (10¹⁹), 720.7 vs 720.0 km/s (2×10²⁰) (numerical)

**Validation.**

- VAL-TAU-001: τ of single, blended, saturated, damped, under-resolved and periodic lines vs exact-Voigt oracle; ∫τ du; τ0; wing τ=1 width — **pass** · 8/8 checks; point sampling max rel τ 5.0e-05, max |ΔF| 1.8e-05

## SCI-ION-001

**Photoionisation equilibrium and the neutral-amount control** — ✓ verified · domain: atomic / IGM

**Claim.** In the highly ionised IGM, photoionisation balances recombination: n_HI Γ_HI = α(T) n_e n_p, so n_HI ≈ α(T) n_e n_H / Γ_HI ∝ Δ² T^(−0.7) / Γ_HI. Changing the UV background rescales n_HI (and τ) by 1/Γ_HI; it does not move lines or change their τ-shape.

**Equations.**

$$ n_{\rm HI} \simeq \frac{\alpha_A(T)\,n_e\,n_{\rm H}}{\Gamma_{\rm HI}},\qquad \alpha_A \simeq 4.2\times10^{-13}\,(T/10^4\,{\rm K})^{-0.7}\ {\rm cm^3\,s^{-1}} $$

**Convention.** case-A recombination (optically thin IGM); n_e = 1.163 n_H (H and He fully ionised, Y_P = 0.2454, Planck 2018)

**Teaching representation.** "neutral amount" control in the core path (Beat 6); the UV background and "bleaching" (gas outline stays, ink fades as Γ rises) only in the Beat 6 microscope

**Validity.** n_HI ≪ n_H (forest; not self-shielded LLS/DLAs)

**Assumptions.** ionisation equilibrium (recombination time ≪ Hubble time is NOT true at mean density; equilibrium is still set by photoionisation, which is fast); He fully ionised (n_e/n_H = 1.081 with helium singly ionised to 1.163 fully ionised, for Y_P = 0.2454; a 7 % systematic)

**Deliberate simplifications / exaggerations.**

- The teaching control changes N_HI directly, holding density, temperature and position fixed; real UV changes also heat the gas.

**Sources.**

- primary: Hui, L. & Gnedin, N. Y. 1997, MNRAS 292, 27–42, 'Equation of state of the photoionized intergalactic medium' — Eq. (12): α ≈ 4×10⁻¹³ (T/10⁴ K)^−0.7 cm³ s⁻¹; Appendix A fit ✓
- primary: McQuinn, M. 2016, ARA&A 54, 313–362, 'The Evolution of the Intergalactic Medium' — §2.1, Eq. (2): x_HI = α_A n_e/Γ ✓
- secondary: Meiksin, A. A. 2009, Rev. Mod. Phys. 81, 1405–1469, 'The physics of the intergalactic medium' — §III.A.1, Eqs. (40)–(42) ✓
- secondary: Draine, B. T. 2011, Physics of the Interstellar and Intergalactic Medium (Princeton University Press) — §14.2, Eq. (14.3): α_A ≈ 4.13e-13 at 10⁴ K ✓

**Implementation.** `science/js/lyaphys.js, science/data/toy/zeldovich3d.py` — alphaA, neOverNH, neutralFraction, nHIRelative

## SCI-DEG-001

**The "same shadow" configurations** — ✓ verified · domain: inference

**Claim.** A constructed degeneracy example, not a model of typical forest absorbers: (i) one unusually hot, idealised compact gas clump (T = 4.5×10⁴ K, Hubble width 2.23 km/s — about 7 kpc proper, far more compact than typical forest gas — N = 2.5×10¹⁴, at rest); (ii) two cold clouds (T = 10⁴ K, Hubble width 12.8 km/s each, 78 km/s apart in Hubble flow, 9.75×10¹³ each, approaching at ±24.9 km/s); (iii) one cold cloud stretched along the line (T = 10⁴ K, Hubble width 11.15 km/s, N = 2.5×10¹⁴) whose smooth extra velocity across 1σ (5.988 km/s) is computed from (i), not tuned: it is the value that gives (iii) the same total Doppler parameter as (i), b_tot² = 2kT/m_H + 2σ_u² = (27.431 km/s)², with the same column. At S/N = 20 per 2.5 km/s pixel with perfect resolution the three Lyα lines are not significantly distinguishable (Δχ² ≈ 2.8 for the blend over 121 pixels); the blend shows by S/N = 50 (Δχ² ≈ 17) and grows as (S/N)², while (iii) stays at Δχ² ≤ 0.002 at every S/N up to 200, in Lyα and in Lyβ. In this constructed model (i) and (iii) are degenerate in every H I Lyman-series line: for a Gaussian clump with a smooth (linear) velocity field the H I profile is a Voigt profile fixed by b_tot and N alone. These are two different kinds of degeneracy. The blend (ii) is measurement-limited: higher S/N, resolution or wavelength coverage can break it. Heat against smooth motion, (i) against (iii), is information-limited for hydrogen: every H I line depends only on the line-of-sight distribution of velocity and optical depth, in which thermal and smooth bulk broadening of one species are the same Gaussian, so another H I line gives no independent distinction — a line of a different mass does (SCI-DEG-002). The blend hides because its two components overlap inside the saturated Lyα core, where the transmitted flux is near zero however the optical depth is split (SCI-SAT-001); Lyβ, with a smaller f λ, is not saturated there and separates it (SCI-DEG-002). What remains of (iii)'s difference is numerical: the clumps are cut at ±5σ (exact-Voigt path, max |ΔF| 4e-06), and the app adds its Voigt approximation's own error (max |ΔF| 4e-05; SCI-VOIGT-002).

**Equations.**

$$ \Delta\chi^2 = \sum_k \bigl(F^{(n)}_k - F^{(i)}_k\bigr)^2/\sigma_F^2 $$
$$ b_{\rm tot}^2 = \frac{2kT}{m_{\rm H}} + 2\sigma_u^2,\quad \sigma_u = s_u + \delta v,\qquad \delta v^{\rm (iii)} = \sqrt{\bigl(s_u^{\rm (i)}\bigr)^2 + \tfrac12\bigl(b_T^{\rm (i)\,2} - b_T^{\rm (iii)\,2}\bigr)} - s_u^{\rm (iii)} $$

**Convention.** noise-free Δχ² against configuration (i), σ_F = 1/(S/N) per 2.5 km/s pixel; configurations defined in velocity space (single source science/validation/degeneracy/configs.json, written by science/tools/same_shadow_configs.py), so they do not depend on the cosmology

**Teaching representation.** predict → reveal → break the tie (Beat 13)

**Validity.** (ii) against (i) — only at the stated S/N and resolution; (i) against (iii) — any S/N and resolution, in H I absorption alone (every Lyman-series line), for this constructed model's Gaussian clumps with smooth (linear) velocity fields

**Assumptions.** white noise as in SCI-OBS-002; perfect resolution

**Deliberate simplifications / exaggerations.**

- (i) and (ii) are chosen by hand; (iii) is computed from (i) by the matching condition
- idealised Gaussian clumps, not typical forest absorbers

**Sources.**

- primary: Rauch, M., Sargent, W. L. W., Womble, D. S. & Barlow, T. A. 1996, ApJ 467, L5, 'Temperature and Kinematics of C IV Absorption Systems' — §3, Eq. (1) (arXiv p. 5): b_i² = b_b² + 2kT/m_i — a bulk width common to all species and a thermal width scaling as m^(−½); the paper separates temperature from bulk motion with ions of different mass — with lines of one mass, Eq. (1) cannot separate T from b_b (our inference) ✓
- primary: Meiksin, A. A. 2009, Rev. Mod. Phys. 81, 1405–1469, 'The physics of the intergalactic medium' — §II.A, Eqs. (10)–(11): b = (2kT/m_a)^½; a kinematic component adds in quadrature ✓

**Oracle.**  independent recomputation with wofz (science/oracle/degeneracy_oracle.py) (numerical)

**Implementation.** `science/tools/same_shadow_configs.py, science/js/lyaphys.js, app/src/scenes/b13-same-shadow.js` — same_shadow_configs, parcelToCells, b13tau

**Validation.**

- VAL-DEG-001: (iii) from the matching rule; same-shadow Δχ² in Lyα and Lyβ at S/N 20–200, browser vs exact-Voigt oracle — **pass** · 13/13 checks; (iii) constructed by the matching rule (dv = 5.9883 km/s, b_tot = 27.4306 km/s for both); Lyα Δχ²(ii) at S/N 20 / 50 / 100 / 200: 2.79 / 17.4 / 70 / 279, Lyβ 103 at S/N 20; Δχ²(iii) ≤ 9e-06 exact-Voigt, ≤ 2e-03 as the app draws it (S/N ≤ 200, Lyα and Lyβ); max |ΔF| vs an independent calculation 3.6e-05

**Scenes using this claim** (derived): Beat 13 · Same shadow

**Notes.** Correction found by VAL-DEG-001 (2026-10-03): an early exploratory figure and the first draft of Beat 13 quoted Δχ² ≈ 3.4–3.5 and 0.8, computed with parcels truncated at ±3σ (an early prototype). For the stated Gaussian parcels the values are 2.9 and 0.9; the app now integrates parcels to ±5σ and agrees with the independent calculation to |ΔF| < 4e-5. That exploratory image is not part of the app; its caption numbers are superseded by this entry. Later (2026-10-03) the configurations were re-expressed in velocity space with rounded values (single source configs.json); Δχ² moved from 2.93/0.89 to the values above. Numbers in prose are now filled from the report by the build. 2026-10-05: (iii)'s extra velocity, previously set by hand (6.2 km/s, which left it measurably different from (i): Δχ² 0.87 at S/N 20, 5.4 at 50, growing as (S/N)²), is now computed by science/tools/same_shadow_configs.py from the matching condition b_tot(iii) = b_tot(i); VAL-DEG-001 checks the rule, Lyα and Lyβ, and S/N 20–200.

## SCI-DEG-002

**What breaks the degeneracy** — ✓ verified · domain: inference

**Claim.** Thermal width scales as m^(−½) while bulk motion broadens all species alike, so a heavier ion's line in the same gas separates heat from motion (Si IV: m ≈ 28 m_H). Lyβ (f λ 6.24× smaller) saturates differently and can, in some cases, expose columns hidden in saturated Lyα.

**Equations.**

$$ b^2 = \frac{2kT}{m} + b^2_{\rm bulk},\qquad \frac{(f\lambda)_{\rm Ly\beta}}{(f\lambda)_{\rm Ly\alpha}} = \frac{0.079142\times1025.722}{0.4164\times1215.67} = 0.160 $$

**Teaching representation.** Si IV and Lyβ toggles (Beat 13)

**Validity.** Illustrative. Si IV separates heat from motion only where silicon is present in the same gas. Lyβ helps only in some cases: in real spectra it lies inside the Lyα forest of lower-redshift gas, so blending and contamination must be modelled; its smaller f λ makes it useful mainly where Lyα saturates; and it needs wavelength coverage down to 1026 Å in the absorber's frame. Like every H I line, Lyβ cannot separate heat from smooth motion (SCI-DEG-001).

**Assumptions.** the gas holds silicon in this ion — the tie-breaker applies only if it does; the metal line traces the same gas (single phase); a common non-thermal (bulk) width shared by both species — an assumption that need not hold everywhere (Rauch et al. 1996), and a stronger one for H I with a metal ion than for two metal ions; illustrative metal column

**Deliberate simplifications / exaggerations.**

- the Si IV column is chosen for visibility
- Lyβ is drawn as a clean line, without the lower-redshift Lyα forest it lies in

**Sources.**

- primary: Rauch, M., Sargent, W. L. W., Womble, D. S. & Barlow, T. A. 1996, ApJ 467, L5, 'Temperature and Kinematics of C IV Absorption Systems' — §3, Eq. (1) (arXiv p. 5): b_i² = b_b² + 2kT/m_i — two ions of different mass (C IV and Si IV) separate temperature from bulk motion ✓
- primary: Kramida, A., Ralchenko, Yu., Reader, J., and NIST ASD Team (2024). NIST Atomic Spectra Database (ver. 5.12), https://physics.nist.gov/asd [accessed 2026-10-02]. National Institute of Standards and Technology, Gaithersburg, MD. — Si IV lines output 1390–1405 Å (ASD v5.12, accessed 2026-10-04): 3s–3p ²P°3/2 at 1393.76 Å (vacuum), f = 0.513 ✓
- primary: NIST Atomic Weights and Isotopic Compositions with Relative Atomic Masses, https://physics.nist.gov/comp — silicon entry; relative atomic masses from 'The AME2012 Atomic Mass Evaluation' (Wang, M. et al. 2012, Chinese Physics C 36(12); DOI 10.1088/1674-1137/36/12/003 as given on the NIST page) — Silicon entry: ²⁸Si 27.9769 u, 92.2 % of silicon ✓
- primary: Kramida, A., Ralchenko, Yu., Reader, J., and NIST ASD Team (2024). NIST Atomic Spectra Database (ver. 5.12), https://physics.nist.gov/asd [accessed 2026-10-02]. National Institute of Standards and Technology, Gaithersburg, MD. — H I lines output 1025–1026 Å (ASD v5.12, accessed 2026-10-03): 1s–3p 2P°3/2 and 2P°1/2, Ritz λ 1025.72182505 / 1025.72296565 Å, f 0.052761 / 0.026380 (multiplet value 0.079142; f-weighted centre 1025.72221 Å) ✓
- primary: Wiese, W. L. & Fuhr, J. R. 2009, J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 38, 565–720, 'Accurate Atomic Transition Probabilities for Hydrogen, Helium, and Lithium'; Publisher's Note: J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 38, 1129 (2009) — Table 6, entry No. 2 (1s–3p), p. 578: f = 0.079142 ✓
- primary: Rauch, M. 1998, ARA&A 36, 267–316, 'The Lyman Alpha Forest in the Spectra of Quasistellar Objects' — §2.4 (arXiv v1 p. 7): 'For stronger Lyα lines the higher order Lyman lines can provide additional constraints when fitted simultaneously'; §3.4 (p. 15): for saturated, blended lines 'simultaneous fits to the higher order Lyman lines (which are less saturated owing to their lower oscillator strengths) can only help to some degree' ✓

## SCI-SIM-003

**Exporting skewers from fake_spectra 2.2.4 — a velocity-convention compatibility note** — ✓ verified · domain: data

**Claim.** During compatibility testing, the velocity returned through the tested export path — fake_spectra 2.2.4, Spectra.get_velocity() on a Gadget-format snapshot — differed from the convention this resource requires (the proper peculiar velocity in km/s, SCI-MAP-002). On a mock snapshot at a = 0.25 with known particle velocities, the returned value was 0.5 of the true peculiar velocity in the pixel of every moving particle, equal to √a — consistent with the √a unit conversion being applied once more than this convention needs. The resource therefore never takes skewer velocities from that path: it constructs the line-of-sight velocity independently from the stored quantities (the toy from its displacement field). One other observation on the same version (2.2.4), for anyone exporting skewers under NumPy 2: get_velocity fails unless its arrays, promoted to float64, are cast back to float32, and HDF5Snapshot.get_npart overflows (2³² × uint32) on headers that store particle counts as uint32, as Gadget does — the mock snapshots store them as int64.

**Equations.**

$$ v_{\rm returned}/v_{\rm pec} = \sqrt{a}\ \text{on the tested path (mock snapshot)};\quad\text{used here: } v_{\rm pec}\ \text{computed independently} $$

**Convention.** v_pec in km/s, proper peculiar velocity (SCI-MAP-002)

**Teaching representation.** none (pipeline guard)

**Validity.** fake_spectra 2.2.4 (PyPI sdist), the tested path only; the √a observation also holds on the upstream master branch as inspected on 2026-10-02. If an upstream issue is filed, this note will link it.

**Sources.**

- primary: fake_spectra (S. Bird), MIT license, https://github.com/sbird/fake_spectra; PyPI package 'fake_spectra' v2.2.4 — spectra.py:954 (second √a); abstractsnapshot.py:114-119 (first √a); under NumPy 2: spectra.py:952-955 (float64 promotion), abstractsnapshot.py:226-228 (get_npart) ✓

**Oracle.** science/oracle/fakespectra_*.py (see closure study) mock snapshot: returned/true = 0.5000 at a = 0.25 (science/validation/closure/mocksnap.json) (numerical)

**Validation.**

- VAL-CLOSURE-FS: browser real-space method vs fake_spectra 2.2.4 on controlled skewers; discrepancies decomposed by source — **pass (declared domain)** · in domain (one velocity per sampling element, b ≥ 2Δu; 25 cases): max |ΔF| 4.9e-03, |Δ⟨F⟩| 2.9e-04, |ΔEW/EW| 2.8e-03, forest P1D 0.17 % (k ≤ 0.05 s/km), 0.32 % (k ≤ 0.1); C8b compared with the exact reference (fake_spectra's own quadrature error exceeds half the tolerance). Outside the domain, stated not tolerated (max |ΔF| per test case, by case name): several velocities inside one real-space sampling element (unresolved velocity structure; C10 is a deliberately exaggerated 1D shell-crossing stress test): C10s0 0.14, C10s1 0.059, C10s2 0.13, C10s3 0.2, C3c 0.089, C4c 0.021; lines narrower than two velocity pixels (b < 2Δu); fixable by oversampling the skewer: C6a 0.45, C6b 0.21, C6c 0.049, C6d 0.46. ## SCI-SIM-TOY-001

**The toy Zel'dovich volume used by the canonical prototype** — ✓ verified · domain: teaching data

**Claim.** The 3D gas, sightline and parcels in this resource come from a declared toy, not a simulation: a 256³ Zel'dovich displacement of a Gaussian field over 20 Mpc/h (P(k) ∝ k⁻² e^(−k²R²), R = 0.075 Mpc/h, ψ_rms = 0.36 Mpc/h), linear peculiar velocities v = f aHψ with f = Ω_m(z)^0.55 (no free velocity scaling), T = T0 Δ^(γ−1) with T0 = 1.3×10⁴ K, γ = 1.5, Planck 2018 cosmology, and n_HI from SCI-ION-001. Γ_HI is tuned so ⟨F⟩ = 0.68 on the chosen sightline (SCI-CTX-003); the tuned value (2.41×10⁻¹² s⁻¹) is 3.0× the measured 0.8×10⁻¹² s⁻¹, so the toy's absolute ionisation is not a physical claim. The skewer file also carries the generating code's own τ (exact Voigt) for the reference view.

**Convention.** the mapping conventions of SCI-MAP-001 and SCI-MAP-003; LOS along the box x-axis; peculiar velocities computed from the displacement field (never from fake_spectra's get_velocity, SCI-SIM-003)

**Teaching representation.** the 3D volume (Beat 0, 20 × 8 × 8 Mpc/h around the beam), the zoomed parcel (Beat 1), the three parcels (Beats 6–8), the forest (Beats 11–12)

**Validity.** teaching only

**Assumptions.** Zel'dovich approximation; no hydrodynamics; no shocks; no pressure beyond a Gaussian filter

**Deliberate simplifications / exaggerations.**

- Rescaling τ to an observed mean flux is standard practice in simulation analysis (fake_spectra ships a mean-flux rescaler); here it is done through Γ_HI.

**Sources.**

- primary: Becker, G. D., Hewett, P. C., Worseck, G. & Prochaska, J. X. 2013, MNRAS 430, 2067–2081, 'A refined measurement of the mean transmitted flux in the Lyα forest over 2 < z < 5 using composite quasar spectra' — Table 2: ⟨F⟩ = 0.6966 (z = 2.95), 0.6670 (z = 3.05) ✓

## SCI-REP-003

**Parcels are a teaching decomposition of a continuous sightline** — ✓ verified · domain: representation

**Claim.** The three parcels a, b, c summarise three n_HI peak regions of the real toy sightline (HI-weighted position, width, column, temperature, velocity and gradient). They are not discrete clouds; Beat 8 dissolves them back into cells. A parcel has a size along the beam, so the velocity spread across it widens its line too (the physics is SCI-MAP-006). Beat 6 isolates the declared terms by setting the parcel's own peculiar-velocity gradient to zero (dv/dx = 0 there), so its size term is the Hubble flow alone, b_size = √2·aH·σ_x; for the parcel it starts from, b_size = 23.8 km/s against a thermal 21.4 km/s, so the drawn line is 32.0 km/s wide (b) — Beat 6's figure names both parts, and "show the physics" prints each and the drawn line's own width. The same toy parcel with its own gradient (-70 km/s per Mpc/h: infall, partly cancelling the Hubble flow), as Beats 7–8 use it, has b_size = 9.1 km/s and b = 23.3 km/s.

**Equations.**

$$ b^2 \simeq b_{\rm thermal}^2 + b_{\rm size}^2,\qquad b_{\rm size} = \sqrt{2}\,\left|aH + \tfrac{dv}{dx}\right|\sigma_x $$

**Convention.** computed once in science/data/toy/zeldovich3d.py (decompose)

**Teaching representation.** Beats 6–8 (and Beat 13's clouds)

**Validity.** always declared

**Assumptions.** Gaussian thermal and spatial profiles (the damping wings aside)

**Deliberate simplifications / exaggerations.**

- Gaussian parcel shape

**Oracle.**  Beat 8 reports the largest flux difference between the 3-parcel and full calculations; VAL-ORTH-001 checks the width Beat 6 prints (check)

**Implementation.** `science/data/toy/zeldovich3d.py` — decompose

**Validation.**

- VAL-ORTH-001: Beat 6's four teaching dimensions stay separate: place, own motion, temperature and neutral amount each changed alone across its control's domain (read from the manifest), checked on the parcel's cells (u, b, N) and on its optical depth (lyaphys parcelTau, measured with lineMoments: centre, FWHM, area) on a fine grid and on the scene's own grid (the comparison it prints); what it prints about the width (b6reading): thermal b, the size term √2·aH·σ_x, and the drawn line's b and peak measured on its drawn grid, against the fine grid and the quadrature sum; flux nonlinearity under saturation recorded, not tested — **pass** · 91/91 checks over 18 one-variable changes (cells and τ, fine grid and the scene's grid): place and motion move the centre by aH·Δx and Δv (max error 4e-07 km/s) at fixed FWHM and area; temperature changes FWHM² by 4 ln2 Δ(b²) (max rel. error 1e-04) at fixed centre and area; amount scales τ exactly (max rel. 2e-15) at fixed centre and FWHM. The width the scene prints is the drawn line's: heat alone b = 21.4 km/s and the parcel's size 23.8 km/s add in quadrature to the drawn 32.0 km/s (max rel. error 2e-04; peak 3e-04). Flux is not linear (recorded): N_HI ×2 gives τ area ×2 but equivalent width ×1.19 (τ₀ = 4.4); T ×2 at fixed N_HI changes it ×1.13

## SCI-REP-005

**Ink is optical depth, and the ink rendering performs Beer–Lambert** — ✓ verified · domain: representation

**Claim.** "Ink" has one meaning throughout: a contribution to optical depth τ, laid in velocity space (Beats 6–13); neutral atoms are drawn as dark dots and motions as arrows, never called ink. The ribbon is rendered by compositing ink layers of opacity 1 − e^(−τᵢ) over a backlight C₀, which yields the transmitted fraction (C − C_ink)/(C₀ − C_ink) = Π e^(−τᵢ) = e^(−Στᵢ): the picture performs the rule it teaches (checked pixel by pixel, VAL-REND-001).

**Equations.**

$$ C \leftarrow C\,(1-\alpha_i) + C_{\rm ink}\,\alpha_i,\ \ \alpha_i = 1 - e^{-\tau_i}\ \Rightarrow\ \dfrac{C - C_{\rm ink}}{C_0 - C_{\rm ink}} = \prod_i e^{-\tau_i} $$

**Teaching representation.** Beat 10 light table — the layered ribbon over a warm backlight; the light that gets through also lights the paper around the ribbon, with a strength at each colour equal to the transmitted fraction there (a saturated trough casts no light); paper fibres show only in that light (VT-FLUX-LIGHT). Beat 12's optical-depth band uses the same compositing for the total τ

**Validity.** exact for black ink

**Assumptions.** ink colour ≈ black

**Oracle.**   (identity)

**Implementation.** `app/src/scenes/b10-light.js` — b10ribbon, beerLambert

**Validation.**

- VAL-REND-001: the light table performs Beer–Lambert (Beat 10): each ribbon pixel's transmitted fraction, read back from the rendered canvas, equals e^(−τ) at that colour — **pass** · Beat 10 ribbon read back from the canvas: max |T − e^(−τ)| 2.1e-03 over 1000 columns (8-bit bound 2.1e-03); mean 9.0e-04

**Scenes using this claim** (derived): Beat 6 · Where does one parcel land?, Beat 9 · Ink adds, Beat 10 · Light multiplies

## SCI-REP-007

**The stretching ribbon and the written shadows (Beat 5 representation)** — ✓ verified · domain: representation

**Claim.** In Beat 5 the quasar's light is a ribbon carrying its own labels (the wavelength each part left with), laid against a ruler of wavelength measured where the light is now, starting at 0 Å, so the stretch by (1 + z_q)/(1 + z_here) is drawn exactly (anchored at zero, every interval scaled). Lyα of the gas being passed is a fixed mark at 1215.67 Å. The gas along the line of sight is a schematic continuous field, not a set of separate clouds: a seeded Gaussian random field in ln Δ (correlation length ~7 Mpc/h comoving, σ = 0.9; far coarser than real structure, chosen to be visible on a 4.5 Gpc/h path), quieter near the quasar, with three density peaks set exactly for the narration (the selected one, placed where the toy stretch's deepest absorption falls on the forest's own wavelength scale, so its shadow has the same wavelength in Beats 5, 11 and 12; and z = 2.90, 2.81). Every cell writes at its own Lyα with strength ∝ Δ² (photoionisation equilibrium, SCI-ION-001) × ((1+z)/4)^1.6, normalised so ⟨F⟩ = 0.74 over z = 2–3; the forest therefore thins toward low z. Density peaks (Δ > 2.2, with their surroundings Δ > 1.3) are the "structures" the narration names and the reader can select. What each cell writes is drawn ~60× wider than a real forest line (6 Å Doppler width when written, versus ~0.1 Å for b = 25 km/s); shadows combine by Beer–Lambert. The close-up of the mark is magnified ~20×. The surface spectrum is continuum-normalised; the quasar's Lyα emission (a schematic bump) is drawn only with "show the physics". The light packet's drawn wavelength is proportional to its true stretch. Path positions are comoving distances (SCI-RED-004).

**Convention.** SCI-RED-001, SCI-RED-005

**Teaching representation.** Beat 5

**Validity.** representation rule

**Deliberate simplifications / exaggerations.**

- No colours are painted on the ribbon; ultraviolet and visible light are not distinguished.
- The close-up keeps a pencil trail of the drift of the quasar's own Lyα (and a cinnabar one for the selected shadow) from the Lyα mark — a record of motion, drawn only while it fits the close-up.

**Implementation.** `app/src/scenes/b05-stretched.js` — R5, b5field, b5sched, sceneStretched

**Validation.**

- VAL-RED-001: frames and redshift: χ(z) and z(χ) vs scipy (Planck 2018 and old toy cosmology), λ_obs = λ_rest(1+z) and its reverse, quasar frame blueward, log-λ stretch = velocity on the SCI-MAP-004 axis, the forest written along the way (λ_emit, λ_here = 1215.67 Å at z_abs, λ_obs, ordering) — **pass** · 6/6 checks; χ(z) vs scipy max rel 8e-11; z(χ) inverse 2e-09; frame conversions exact to 1e-16; Lyα at z = 3 → 4862.68 Å
